senses.gloss: f.(b. h. עוֹלֵלוֹת pl., = מְעוֹ׳; עָלַל) [that which is searched after,] gleaning reserved for the poor; in gen. small single bunch (on a single branch, or hanging down directly from the trunk), opp. to אשכול.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Peah 7:4">Peah VII, 4</cite> <he>איזהו ע׳</he>, v. <cite ref="K01381"><he>כָּתֵף</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Peah 7:4">Ib.</cite> <he>ע׳ בארכובה</he> a bunch on the knee of a vine.
Ib. גרגר יחידי … ע׳ (Mish. ed. עוֹלֵלוֹת pl.) single berries … are considered gleanings (belong to the poor); Sifra K’dosh., Par. 1, ch. III; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 29:2">Gen. R. s. 29</cite> <he>ראה עוללה אחת וכ׳</he> saw a single bunch (that wag ripe), and said a blessing over it; <he>כדאי הע׳ וכ׳</he> this single bunch is worth saying a blessing over it.

Lam. R. to I, 12 (ref. to עולל ib.) קטף עוֹלְלָתִי he cut my last bunch (destroyed me entirely), v. עוֹלְלָא.—Pl. עוֹלֵלוֹת. Sifra l. c.; Peah VII, 7 כרם שכולו ע׳ a vineyard in which all grapes grow in small separate bunches.

<cite ref="Mishnah Peah 7:8">Ib. 8</cite> <he>המקדיש … בו הע׳ וכ׳</he> if one consecrates his vineyards before the bunches (which would have been the poor man’s share) were distinguishable on it, they do not belong to the poor.

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 121:1">Midr. Till. to Ps. CXXI</cite> <he>אלקוט עוֹלְלוֹתֶיהָ של גפן</he> (not <he>עלילותי׳</he>) I will pluck the very gleanings of the vines; <he>ואת לקחת עד הע׳ וכ׳</he> (read <he>לקטת</he>) but thou hast plucked the last grapes.

<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 3:2">Esth. R. to I, 9</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 3:12">Is. III, 12</cite>, and <cite ref="Leviticus 9:10">Lev. IX, 10</cite>) <he>מקטפין עוֹלְלוֹתֵיהֶן</he> they (the officers) cut their gleanings (rob the people of their last belongings); a. fr.
